title: Real-Time Audio Thread Safety
summary: Patterns and anti-patterns for audio thread safety in JUCE plugins.
description:
## Overview

The audio thread (processBlock) runs in a real-time context where allocations, locks, and blocking operations are forbidden. This entry covers the essential patterns for maintaining real-time safety.

## Core Rules

### Forbidden Operations
- **No heap allocations**: `new`, `delete`, `std::vector::push_back()`, `juce::String` construction
- **No system calls**: file I/O, network, mutex lock attempts
- **No blocking operations**: `std::mutex::lock()`, `std::condition_variable::wait()`
- **No unbounded loops**: must have fixed iteration limits

### Required Patterns

```cpp
void processBlock(juce::AudioBuffer<float>& buffer, juce::MidiBuffer&) override {
    juce::ScopedNoDenormals noDenormals;  // Always first
    
    // Use pre-allocated member buffers
    // Use std::atomic<bool> for cross-thread flags
    // Call getNextValue() per-sample for smoothed parameters
}
```

## Failure Modes

| ID | Symptom | Cause | Prevention |
|----|---------|-------|------------|
| FM-01 | Dropouts, crashes | Heap allocation | Pre-allocate in prepareToPlay() |
| FM-04 | CPU spikes | Denormals | ScopedNoDenormals |
| FM-07 | Intermittent crashes | Non-atomic callbacks | Use atomic<bool> flags |
source: VST Playbook v7 failure modes + JUCE documentation
